The must-sees

8 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Market · 1928

    Central Market

    It opened in 1928, designed by Alexandre Soler i March and Francesc Guàrdia i Vial. A weathervane parrot, the cotorra, sits on one of its domes.

    Look for

    Across the street stands the Gothic Silk Exchange, and the church of the Santos Juanes backs onto the market square.

  2. 02
    Culture · 1998

    City of Arts and Sciences

    Santiago Calatrava designed most of the complex, and its first building, L’Hemisfèric, opened in 1998. It was built in the former bed of the Turia, diverted after a flood.

    Look for

    L’Hemisfèric is shaped like a giant eye: its reflection in the pool completes the eye, and its shell opens like an eyelid.

  3. 03
    Viewpoint

    Micalet Tower

    It was built between the late 14th and early 15th centuries. Its name comes from its great bell, Miquel, and a long spiral stair leads to the bell terrace.

    Look for

    From the top, look down on the cathedral’s octagonal lantern and the glazed-tile domes of the old town.

  4. 04
    Palace

    Palace of the Marqués de Dos Aguas

    The rococo doorway was carved in the 18th century by Ignacio Vergara from a design by Hipólito Rovira. The palace now houses the National Ceramics Museum.

    Look for

    The two giants pour water from jars, a pun on the family title: Dos Aguas means two waters.

  5. 05
    Fortress · 1398

    Serranos Towers

    They were built at the end of the 14th century as part of the medieval walls. The Fallas season opens here each year with the Crida, the call to the festival.

    Look for

    Walk round to the city side: the towers are open there, so attackers who took them would find no cover.

  6. 06
    Building

    Silk Exchange

    It was built at the end of the 15th century, when Valencia was one of the richest trading cities of the Mediterranean. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

    Look for

    Look up at the gargoyles on the outer walls: monsters, musicians and some decidedly rude figures.

  7. 07
    Square

    Town Hall Square

    This is the stage of the Fallas: every day at 2 pm from 1 to 19 March the mascletà, a thunderous daytime fireworks display, shakes the square. The largest falla is burned here on the last night.

    Look for

    Find the City Hall balcony: each 9 October the old Senyera banner is lowered from it, and it must never bow on the way down.

  8. 08
    Church

    Valencia Cathedral

    Building began in the 13th century on the site of the city’s main mosque after the Christian conquest. A chapel keeps an agate cup venerated as the Holy Grail, and every Thursday the Water Tribunal meets at its Apostles’ Door.

    Look for

    Over the Romanesque Palau Door, find fourteen carved heads, said to be seven couples who resettled the city after the conquest.
